public_rationale: The 117 MW ceiling is not established. Epoch's retrospective 369 MW IT estimate challenges it, and Microsoft confirms revenue-generating operation in April. However, neither establishes how much total facility capacity was commissioned during startup. Contemporaneous reporting describes limited operations, and full operation was announced in June. These records leave the publication-time upper bound unsettled; they do not justify treating the old permit figure as a verified ceiling.
limitations: Rated capacity and the commissioned portion of a startup facility may differ.
The permit basis could not be independently read.
IT power is not the same measurement as total facility power.
The June announcement cannot establish the May operating quantity.

statement.document_title: Where Are All The Data Centers?

our_interpretation: The plain reading is an approximate upper bound on commissioned operating capacity at the Wisconsin site, not a measurement of momentary electricity consumption.
The surrounding comparison treats MW as total facility capacity rather than critical IT capacity.
The context explicitly uses April 2026 observations to describe the state at publication, so the target period is April 1 through May 12, 2026.
Startup activity can establish that some equipment was operating without establishing that the building's entire rated capacity was commissioned.
An older permit's design or backup-generator figure cannot establish the running-capacity ceiling unless its scope and continuing applicability are verified.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable operating records establish that the site's commissioned capacity remained no greater than approximately 117 MW at publication.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Dated records establish that materially more than 117 MW of total facility capacity was commissioned and operating at the site by publication.
